gloss: decorative knife cuts (made in food for appearance)

definitions.gloss: decorative knife cuts; ornamental scoring of an ingredient
definitions.explanation: Shallow cuts made in an ingredient mainly to make the finished dish look better — a cross-hatch in a shiitake cap, a fan shape in cucumber, diagonal slits in squid. Often improves heat and flavor penetration as well, but appearance is the point.

examples.japanese: {椎茸|しいたけ}に{飾|かざ}り{包丁|ぼうちょう}を{入|い}れる。
examples.english: Score a decorative pattern into the shiitake mushrooms.

examples.japanese: {飾|かざ}り{包丁|ぼうちょう}を{入|い}れるだけで{料理|りょうり}が{見栄|みば}えする。
examples.english: Just adding decorative cuts makes the dish look impressive.

examples.japanese: {煮物|にもの}の{人参|にんじん}に{飾|かざ}り{包丁|ぼうちょう}を{入|い}れて、{花|はな}の{形|かたち}に{仕上|しあ}げた。
examples.english: I cut a decorative pattern into the carrots for the simmered dish, finishing them in a flower shape.

notes:
Always used with {入|い}れる, never with {切|き}る: the cuts are "put into" the ingredient.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {飾|かざ}り{包丁|ぼうちょう}を{入|い}れる: to make decorative cuts
- {飾|かざ}り{切|ぎ}り: decorative cutting (the technique in general)
- {花|はな}{形|がた}に{切|き}る: to cut into a flower shape

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {隠|かく}し{包丁|ぼうちょう}: hidden scoring — made where it will not be seen, for cooking rather than looks
- {切|き}り{込|こ}み: a slit or incision — the plain word for any cut made into something
